channel.title: Daily AI News
channel.description: Twice-daily AI news briefing produced by the daily-ai-news Copilot skill.

item.title: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 4.8 with stronger agentic coding and “honesty” improvements
item.description: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.8, upgrading its top model for coding, agentic workflows, professional work, and uncertainty signaling.

item.title: Microsoft redesigns Microsoft 365 Copilot for faster, more structured workplace AI
item.description: Microsoft introduced a redesigned Microsoft 365 Copilot experience focused on speed, clearer outputs, and task-aware controls.

item.title: CORE proposes faster reasoning improvement through contrastive reflection
item.description: A new arXiv paper introduces Contrastive Reflection, a non-parametric method for improving language-model reasoning by comparing successful and unsuccessful reasoning traces.

item.title: Anthropic raises $65B at a $965B post-money valuation
item.description: Anthropic announced a $65 billion Series H round led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, and Sequoia Capital.

item.title: Figma Make can now work directly in production codebases
item.description: Figma announced beta capabilities that let Figma Make visually edit local production codebases from the Figma desktop app.

item.title: Illinois passes landmark frontier AI safety bill
item.description: Illinois lawmakers passed SB 315, a bill that would require frontier AI companies to publish safety plans and undergo annual independent third-party audits if signed.

item.title: CNN sues Perplexity over alleged unauthorized copying
item.description: CNN filed its first AI copyright lawsuit, accusing Perplexity of unlawfully copying and distributing CNN content.

item.title: YouTube is rolling out prompt-built custom AI video feeds
item.description: YouTube is launching an AI feature that lets users describe the kind of videos they want and pin a generated custom feed to the top of the homepage.

item.title: Google brings Preferred Sources into AI Overviews and AI Mode
item.description: Google is adding Preferred Sources labels, new article carousels, and expanded “Highly Cited” badges to make original and user-selected sources more visible in AI search.
item.category: Summary: Google is adding Preferred Sources labels, new article carousels, and expanded “Highly Cited” badges to make original and user-selected sources more visible in AI search.

item.title: ElevenLabs launches Music v2 for more controllable AI song generation
item.description: ElevenLabs released Music v2, an AI music model that can switch genres mid-track, regenerate sections, and build longer songs by structure.

item.title: Vertu launches a $6,880 AI-agent foldable phone for executives
item.description: Vertu unveiled Alphafold, a luxury foldable phone with a Hermes Agent designed to connect with enterprise tools and coordinate workflows.

item.title: YouTube moves AI labels into more visible places and expands auto-detection
item.description: YouTube is relocating AI disclosure labels below videos and on Shorts while expanding automatic identification of photorealistic AI-generated content.

item.title: OpenAI and Anthropic-linked groups escalate AI regulation politics
item.description: The Verge reports that AI industry-backed political groups have spent millions around a New York congressional race tied to AI safety regulation.

item.title: Robinhood opens trading and payments to AI agents
item.description: Robinhood launched beta support for AI agents that can trade equities and use a dedicated virtual credit card with user-controlled limits.

item.title: OpenAI publishes Codex case study on self-improving tax agents
item.description: OpenAI highlighted work with Thrive and Crete on a Codex-powered tax agent designed to automate filings, improve accuracy, and accelerate tax workflows.

item.title: MUSE-Autoskill proposes lifecycle-managed skills for self-evolving agents
item.description: A new arXiv paper introduces MUSE-Autoskill, a framework for agents to create, remember, manage, evaluate, and refine reusable skills.

item.title: Snowflake signs $6B AWS deal for AI compute
item.description: Snowflake signed a five-year, $6 billion agreement with AWS to secure compute capacity, including access to Amazon’s Graviton CPUs for AI workloads.

item.title: Cognition raises $1B at a $25B pre-money valuation
item.description: Cognition, maker of the Devin autonomous software engineer, raised more than $1 billion as it reports rapid enterprise growth.

item.title: ElevenLabs launches Music v2 for genre-switching AI songs
item.description: ElevenLabs released Music v2, a music-generation model that can switch genres mid-track and regenerate individual song sections.

item.title: Meta rolls out app subscriptions and tests paid Meta AI plans
item.description: Meta launched Plus subscriptions for Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp while preparing Meta One AI plans with expanded compute and generation limits.

item.title: YouTube will automatically label significant AI-generated videos
item.description: YouTube will now use internal systems to apply AI labels to videos containing significant photorealistic AI, instead of relying only on creator disclosure.

item.title: OpenAI outlines 2026 election information safeguards
item.description: OpenAI published its 2026 election safeguards, emphasizing access to election information, support for cyber defenders, and AI transparency.

item.title: Robinhood now lets AI agents trade stocks
item.description: Robinhood launched beta support for AI agents that can analyze portfolios and place stock trades from a dedicated, pre-funded wallet.

item.title: Google introduces Gemini for Science
item.description: Google announced Gemini for Science, an experimental agentic AI suite for hypothesis generation, computational testing, and literature review.

item.title: YouTube will automatically label significant photorealistic AI videos
item.description: YouTube is making AI-content disclosures more visible and will automatically apply labels when its systems detect significant photorealistic AI use.

item.title: MobileMoE pushes mixture-of-experts models onto smartphones
item.description: A new arXiv paper introduces MobileMoE, a family of sub-billion-active-parameter MoE language models optimized for on-device deployment.

item.title: New paper warns RLHF can amplify “alignment tampering”
item.description: An ICML 2026 paper argues that RLHF can amplify undesired behavior when model-generated preference data mixes quality signals with hidden biases.

item.title: DuckDuckGo installs spike after Google’s AI Search overhaul
item.description: DuckDuckGo says U.S. app installs rose after Google’s I/O Search redesign pushed AI agents and AI-generated answers more deeply into search.

item.title: Fabricated AI citations are appearing in biomedical papers
item.description: A large audit of biomedical literature found fabricated references in peer-reviewed papers rising sharply since 2023.

item.title: Anthropic expands Claude capacity with SpaceX compute deal
item.description: Anthropic says a new SpaceX compute partnership lets it raise Claude Code and API usage limits.

item.title: MixT compression cuts LLM peak inference memory by 60.4%
item.description: A new arXiv paper introduces Tensor Mixture, a tensor-structured compression method for dense linear layers in LLMs.

item.title: Beijing study links GenAI exposure to an urban “high-skill trap”
item.description: Researchers used 5 million job postings to study how GenAI exposure affects intra-urban inequality in Beijing.

item.title: Sam Altman softens “AI jobs apocalypse” expectations
item.description: Sam Altman said he no longer expects the kind of near-term jobs apocalypse some AI leaders have predicted.

item.title: Enterprises want agents, but most are not operationally ready
item.description: MIT Technology Review Insights reports a gap between enterprise interest in agentic AI and the infrastructure needed to support it.

item.title: Google AI Overviews stumble on a simple date question
item.description: Google’s AI Overviews reportedly answered “is 2027 next year” incorrectly, citing old social posts about the same error.

item.title: Erin Brockovich launches U.S. AI data center impact map
item.description: Erin Brockovich is tracking U.S. data center projects and local complaints tied to the AI infrastructure boom.

item.title: AI-assisted lawsuits are straining court systems
item.description: The Verge points to reporting that AI-assisted self-filed lawsuits are flooding courts.

item.title: Google CEO says AI is reshaping Search and the open web
item.description: Sundar Pichai told The Verge that Google’s post-I/O AI push marks a new platform-shift phase, with AI Mode moving Search toward generated, interactive result experiences.

item.title: Agentic AI research shifts from model scaling to system scaling
item.description: A new arXiv paper, “From Model Scaling to System Scaling: Scaling the Harness in Agentic AI,” argues that future agent progress depends on verifiable orchestration systems around foundation models.

item.title: Perceptic emerges from stealth with $12M for AI drug discovery
item.description: London-based Perceptic, founded by former Palantir executives, raised a $12 million seed round to automate end-to-end drug discovery workflows for pharmaceutical companies.

item.title: Uber executive says AI spending is getting harder to justify
item.description: Uber president and COO Andrew Macdonald said rising AI coding-tool costs are becoming harder to connect directly to consumer-facing productivity gains.

item.title: xAI’s Grok Build enters the AI coding-agent race
item.description: xAI’s reported Grok Build CLI targets terminal-native software engineering workflows with planning, code editing, command execution, and agentic development features.

item.title: Anthropic-Pentagon clash spotlights AI warfare red lines
item.description: The Verge reported that Anthropic’s dispute with the Pentagon highlights how quickly AI systems are being pulled into military workflows and autonomous warfare debates.

item.title: Erin Brockovich launches map tracking AI data center conflicts
item.description: Erin Brockovich launched a public map and reporting tool to track US data center projects and local complaints tied to the AI infrastructure buildout.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV calls for AI to remain “profoundly human”
item.description: Pope Leo XIV’s first encyclical, “Magnifica Humanitas,” warns that AI could deepen inequality, dehumanize work, and concentrate power unless governed around human dignity.

item.title: OpenAI expands journalism partnerships in Brazil
item.description: OpenAI announced a strategic content partnership with Grupo Folha and Grupo UOL to bring Brazilian journalism into ChatGPT with attribution and transparency.

item.title: Shannon Scaling Law proposes a new theory for LLM degradation
item.description: A new ICML 2026 paper models LLM training as information transmission over a noisy channel to explain why more compute or data can sometimes degrade performance.

item.title: XWind routes AI inference to wind-powered compute
item.description: Researchers proposed “AI Greenferencing,” placing modular AI compute near renewable energy sources and routing inference workloads based on real-time wind availability.

item.title: Vision-language benchmarks may overstate visual grounding
item.description: A CVPR 2026 workshop paper found that some VLM benchmark scores remain surprisingly stable even when large fractions of image tokens are removed.

item.title: OpenRouter raises $113M at reported $1.3B valuation
item.description: OpenRouter raised a $113 million Series B led by CapitalG as demand grows for routing workloads across multiple AI models.

item.title: Human Archive raises $8.2M to collect physical-world AI training data
item.description: Human Archive is paying gig workers, primarily in India, to collect first-person video and sensor data for robotics and physical AI training.

item.title: Gemini Omni Flash shows both progress and deepfake risk
item.description: Google’s Gemini Omni Flash can generate video from multiple input types, with The Verge finding it more capable than Veo in some edits but still glitchy and unsettlingly convincing for deepfakes.

item.title: GitHub Copilot remote control is generally available
item.description: GitHub made remote control for Copilot CLI sessions generally available on github.com and GitHub Mobile.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV calls for AI oversight rooted in human dignity
item.description: Pope Leo XIV’s first encyclical, *Magnifica Humanitas*, uses AI to warn about concentrated power, inequality, war, misinformation, and democratic erosion.

item.title: Microsoft 365 Copilot vulnerability analysis highlights enterprise AI risk
item.description: Cloud Security Alliance analyzed CVE-2026-24299, a Microsoft 365 Copilot command-injection vulnerability that could disclose sensitive organizational information under specific conditions.

item.title: Google pushes deeper into agentic search, Gemini, and AI-first products
item.description: Google CEO Sundar Pichai described a companywide AI reset around Gemini, Search, YouTube, agents, and AI infrastructure after Google I/O 2026.

item.title: UMG and TikTok renew deal with stronger AI music protections
item.description: Universal Music Group and TikTok renewed their global licensing agreement, including commitments to remove unauthorized AI-generated music and improve artist attribution.

item.title: MobileGym targets scalable training and evaluation for mobile AI agents
item.description: A new arXiv paper introduces MobileGym, a browser-hosted environment for mobile-use agents with deterministic state judging and low-cost parallel rollouts.

item.title: Claw-Anything benchmark exposes gaps in always-on personal assistants
item.description: Researchers introduced Claw-Anything, a benchmark for agents with months-long user histories, interdependent services, and GUI/CLI interaction across devices.

item.title: ClickUp lays off 22% while betting on thousands of internal AI agents
item.description: ClickUp cut 22% of its workforce and says it is reallocating toward an AI-driven “100x org” model.

item.title: Uber questions whether AI token spending is paying off
item.description: Uber president Andrew Macdonald said rising AI spending is getting harder to justify without a clearer link to useful shipped features.

item.title: Google’s Gemini Spark and Antigravity updates push agents into everyday workflows
item.description: Google is rolling out Gemini Spark as an always-on agent and expanding Antigravity as an agent-first developer platform.

item.title: Universal Cart shows Google’s bet on AI-mediated shopping
item.description: Google’s Universal Cart aims to let users collect, track, and eventually buy products across Gemini, Search, and other Google surfaces.

item.title: Anthropic’s Pentagon fight highlights how close AI warfare already is
item.description: The Verge reports that Anthropic is trying to preserve limits on mass surveillance and fully autonomous weapons as the Pentagon pushes broader “any lawful use” AI terms.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV calls for AI governance centered on human dignity
item.description: Pope Leo XIV’s first encyclical, *Magnifica Humanitas*, calls for stronger ethical and legal frameworks around AI, labor, warfare, education, and algorithmic power.

item.title: Google I/O 2026: Gemini Omni Debuts — 100 AI Announcements Drop
item.description: Google's most AI-saturated developer conference ever kicked off today, unveiling Gemini Omni and a sweeping overhaul of nearly every Google product with AI.

item.title: AI Captures 45% of All VC Deals in May — $25B Disclosed
item.description: AI startups commanded nearly half of all venture capital activity in May 2026, with 37 of 82 tracked deals totaling $25 billion in disclosed funding.

item.title: EU AI Act High-Risk Enforcement Deadline Approaches — August 2026
item.description: With the EU AI Act's August 2026 enforcement date for high-risk AI systems approaching, global compliance pressure is intensifying for AI companies operating in Europe.

item.title: Governments Demand Pre-Release Model Testing — Major Labs Comply
item.description: The US and other governments are now requiring pre-release regulatory testing for new frontier AI models, with OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic agreeing to provide early regulatory access.

item.title: Google I/O 2026: "The Agentic Gemini Era" Begins
item.description: Google CEO Sundar Pichai declared we are "firmly in the agentic Gemini era," unveiling 50+ announcements including new frontier models, a 24/7 personal AI agent, and a major hardware pivot.

item.title: Tencent Launches Marvis: OS-Level AI Assistant
item.description: Tencent released Marvis, a cross-platform AI assistant operating at the OS level with multi-device support and a local privacy mode.

item.title: AI Startup Funding Reaches $25B in May Alone
item.description: May 2026 has already seen 37 disclosed AI funding deals totaling $25B, continuing a record-breaking year for AI venture capital.

item.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano Omni: Open-Source Multimodal Powerhouse
item.description: NVIDIA released a fully open-source multimodal model supporting video, audio, image, and text in a single system.

item.title: DeepSeek V4 Series Resets Price-Performance Expectations
item.description: DeepSeek V4-Flash and V4-Pro released as open-weight frontier-class models with dramatically lower API pricing than Western equivalents.

item.title: Adobe Photoshop 27.7: Local AI Gets Double Credits
item.description: Adobe shipped a major AI update to Photoshop, doubling generative AI credits for locally-processed operations and emphasizing hybrid cloud/local processing.

item.title: EU AI Act High-Risk Compliance Deadline Approaching: August 2026
item.description: The EU AI Act's full compliance requirements for high-risk AI systems — used in hiring, credit, healthcare, and law enforcement — take effect in August 2026.

item.title: Agentic AI Triggers Liability Gap Debate in US Congress
item.description: The rise of autonomous AI agents is prompting urgent legal debate in the US about who bears liability when an AI agent causes harm — the user, developer, or deployer.

item.title: OpenAI's reasoning model disproves a 1946 Erdős conjecture in discrete geometry
item.description: OpenAI's new reasoning model autonomously disproved the planar unit distance problem first posed by Paul Erdős in 1946 — being called a milestone in AI mathematics.

item.title: Anthropic posts "biggest week ever": Claude Code Auto Mode, Claude Design, Karpathy hire
item.description: Anthropic ran a barrage of releases this week — Claude Code Auto Mode, a new visual collaboration product called Claude Design, and confirmation that Andrej Karpathy is joining to work on Claude pretraining research.

item.title: DeepWeb-Bench and PALS headline this week's arXiv drops
item.description: A wave of new arXiv papers this week pushes harder benchmarks and more sustainable serving methods for frontier models.

item.title: Evolution Strategies revive as a scalable fine-tuning path for billion-parameter LLMs
item.description: New work shows Evolution Strategies can efficiently fine-tune billion-parameter language models, with measurable gains on math reasoning benchmarks.

item.title: Q1 2026: 80% of global venture funding went to AI
item.description: Crunchbase-style data show AI captured $242B of the $300B in global venture funding in Q1 2026 — up from 55% a year earlier — with four companies absorbing roughly 65% of that total.

item.title: Anthropic and OpenAI both launch Wall Street joint ventures for enterprise AI
item.description: In parallel announcements, Anthropic and OpenAI each unveiled joint ventures with major private equity firms to push AI services into hundreds of midsized companies and PE portfolios.

item.title: Alibaba ships Qwen3.7-Max as a "new agent frontier" model
item.description: Alibaba released Qwen3.7-Max with a deliberate focus on agentic capabilities — autonomous reasoning, tool use, and multi-step task solving.

item.title: OpenAI adopts Google's SynthID watermark for AI-generated images
item.description: OpenAI is adopting Google's SynthID watermarking for AI-generated images and shipping a verification tool to detect AI-created content.

item.title: EU AI Act hits hard-enforcement phase; US considers pre-release model vetting
item.description: The EU AI Act is now in active enforcement for high-risk systems, while the White House is reportedly weighing pre-release vetting for advanced AI models.

item.title: Google I/O 2026: Gemini 3.5 Flash, Spark, and Omni unveiled
item.description: Google used its I/O keynote to roll out a new lightweight flagship model, a personal agent, and a "world model" for physical-world simulation.

item.title: OpenAI reasoning model autonomously solves a 1946 Erdős geometry problem
item.description: OpenAI announced a new reasoning system that independently disproved the planar unit-distance problem posed by Paul Erdős in 1946 — reportedly the first time an AI has autonomously resolved a major open mathematical conjecture.

item.title: Anthropic ships Claude Design, hires Karpathy, signs mega cloud deals
item.description: Anthropic had one of the most consequential weeks of its history, pairing product launches with massive infrastructure deals and a marquee hire.

item.title: Penn researchers demonstrate hybrid light-matter particle for optical AI compute
item.description: A University of Pennsylvania team reported a hybrid light-matter quasiparticle that could enable dramatically faster and more energy-efficient AI computation, suggesting a path for optical processors to replace electronic ones on key AI workloads.

item.title: Anthropic acquires Stainless, cutting off a key dev-tools vendor used by OpenAI and Google
item.description: Anthropic acquired developer-tools startup **Stainless**, reportedly for over $300M. Stainless's SDK and API-automation tech was widely used by OpenAI, Google, and Cloudflare; going forward its core products will be Anthropic-only.

item.title: Anduril closes record $5B Series H at $61B valuation
item.description: AI-defense company **Anduril** closed a $5B Series H at a $61B valuation — the largest venture round ever in defense tech — to scale manufacturing of autonomous drones, weapons, and naval systems.

item.title: Pre-release model testing becomes a global norm as enforcement era begins
item.description: Multiple major governments are now requiring pre-release testing and transparency disclosures for frontier AI models, marking a clear shift from voluntary guidelines to active enforcement.

item.title: Google I/O 2026: Gemini Omni, Gemini 3.5 Flash, and Agentic-First Stack Unveiled
item.description: Google used I/O 2026 to roll out two new flagship Gemini models and reorganize its product line around autonomous agents.

item.title: KPMG to Deploy Anthropic's Claude Across Global Tax and Advisory, Training 30,000 Staff
item.description: KPMG will embed Claude into its global tax and advisory platform and stand up a joint Center of Excellence with Anthropic.

item.title: arXiv Imposes One-Year Ban on Authors Who Let LLMs Write Entire Papers
item.description: arXiv's computer science section will ban authors for a year if a submission contains "incontrovertible evidence" the authors did not check LLM-generated content.

item.title: Mercury Hits $5.2B Valuation on $200M Series D as "Bank for AI Startups"
item.description: AI-startup-focused digital bank Mercury raised a $200M Series D led by TCV, lifting its valuation 49% to $5.2B.

item.title: Exa Raises $250M Series C at $2.2B Valuation to Build "Search Engine for AI Agents"
item.description: AI-native search infrastructure company Exa closed a $250M Series C to scale models and infrastructure designed for autonomous agent queries.

item.title: Google Ships Antigravity 2.0 with Desktop App, CLI, SDK, and Voice Control
item.description: Google launched Antigravity 2.0 at I/O 2026, expanding its agentic coding platform with a redesigned desktop app, a new CLI, and an SDK for custom agents.

item.title: EU AI Act's August 2, 2026 Enforcement Deadline Looms, Most Enterprises Unprepared
item.description: With roughly ten weeks to go, analysts warn that the bulk of EU AI Act obligations for high-risk systems will become enforceable on August 2, 2026, while most enterprises lack basic AI inventories.
